subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Lessons Learned: How Failure Drives Progress
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Lessons Learned: How Failure Drives Progress.

hook.text: Every major engineering disaster led to new safety standards. Failure is the most expensive teacher, but the most effective.

buildup.text: The Comet gave us fatigue-safe design. Tacoma Narrows gave us wind tunnel testing. Challenger gave us launch decision protocols.

discovery.text: Failure analysis is now a scientific discipline. Fractography reads broken surfaces like a forensic detective reads a crime scene.

twist.text: Many failures come not from unknown science but from ignored warnings. Human factors kill as often as material defects.

climax.text: Modern design uses safety factors, redundancy, inspection, and fail-safe principles. We build on the lessons of every disaster.

punchline.text: We learn from failure so others don't repeat it. That's progress.

quiz.question: What is fractography?
options: A method for welding broken metal parts back together
The scientific analysis of broken surfaces to determine how and why failure occurred
A computer simulation that predicts where fractures will start in a design
